subject: Anthropology
title: Epigenetics and Evolution
description: A micro-lesson that makes Epigenetics and Evolution usable.

hook.text: A famine in one generation changes gene expression in the next. Your grandparents' diet shapes your biology.

buildup.text: Epigenetics studies changes in gene expression that don't alter DNA itself but can be inherited across generations.

discovery.text: Environmental stressors like famine, pollution, and trauma can switch genes on or off in offspring.

twist.text: This means the environment shapes heredity more than we thought. Lamarck wasn't entirely wrong after all.

climax.text: Epigenetics adds a new layer to evolution. Genes aren't just destiny — they respond to the world around them.

punchline.text: Your genes listen to the environment.

quiz.question: What does epigenetics study?
options: Heritable changes in gene expression without DNA alteration

details.summary: Epigenetics studies how gene expression is modified without changing DNA sequences — through chemical markers that turn genes on or off. Environmental exposures, diet, and stress can alter epigenetic patterns, and some changes may be transmitted across generations.
details.whyItMatters: Epigenetics reveals that genes are not destiny. Environmental experiences can alter gene expression and potentially pass effects to offspring, adding a new mechanism to evolution that supplements natural selection and blurs the nature-nurture.
takeaways: Epigenetics modifies gene expression without changing DNA sequences
Environmental factors like diet and stress alter epigenetic patterns
Some epigenetic changes may be transmitted across generations

faq.question: How does epigenetics differ from genetics?
faq.answer: Genetics studies DNA sequences — the code itself. Epigenetics studies how genes are regulated — which genes are turned on or off in different cells and conditions. Two identical DNA sequences can produce very different outcomes depending on their epigenetic states.

faq.question: Can epigenetic changes really be inherited?
faq.answer: Evidence suggests some epigenetic marks survive across generations in animals and possibly humans. Studies of famine survivors show health effects in children and grandchildren. However, the extent and mechanisms of transgenerational epigenetic inheritance in humans remain actively debated.
